title: Finite bit construction: two-copy scatter saves 120 ADDs (no new kappa)
body:
Two simultaneously live ZERO-frame copies let the fixed PR1062 scatter share pair sums, reducing its complete scalar word from **11,500 to 11,380 ADDs** while restoring each copied value before its chronological ERASE. This needs a second copied temporary and a replacement for the native immutable-temporary rule. It is a finite interface construction, **not native supplier admission or a new kappa**.

The package proves the arbitrary-dirty block identity and exhausts all **2,620 disjoint pair/singleton partitions** of the nine totals: maximum saving **120**, with **105 optima**. This is only the defined block class, not arbitrary two-temporary circuits. Nine rank-seven COPYs, all persistent frame paths and local rank mass 5,129 are unchanged. Peak live copies rise 1→2; reverse positive bound rises 5,911,840→6,248,884. Both inherited algebraic precision expressions remain strictly within their caps. Physical workspace/hosting and migrated native precision remain open.

Validation: registered Python 3.12 replay passes; all 661 dirty columns pass in both directions. A separate implementation checks equality of the original/candidate signed integer matrices, subset-DP optimality and fraction-free frame ranks. All 2,620 partitions have their dirty scatter boundary checked; nine test groups cover gate omissions, early ERASE, wrong signed restoration, illegal roles, accounting and receipt/source corruption, plus read-only relocation. Selected-record integrity and binding-only baseline checks pass. No selected cold replay, native two-copy compilation, outer assembly, Lean proof, independent human review or hosted-CI pass is claimed.

Reproduce:
```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-two-copy-scatter
```

Research base `5e554ff58d01921747d27177045c0061f31e1ad1`; PR1062 input head `cd016e5dcd5ba28dafa3f3b4eeef003a38e6a11b`. Exact consumed Git/SHA pins, task/changed-scope declaration, proof, full local invoice, overlap receipt and limitations are in `research/bit-two-copy-scatter/`. The scope changed from the helper's H2/K card because PR1194/1306 already cover its immediate semantic boundary. [Discussion 1687](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1687) records the claim and outcome. Source inputs and selected record are unchanged on refreshed main `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`.

Credit Sagar Thakrar's PR1062 construction, the PR967/926 helper lineage, Aaron Wang's PR1015 and Ross Richardson's PR923 blocks, DreamingOfClouds' PR589, eumemic's PR555/checkers, Dylan Crow's exporter, woklerx's live-copy/late-mixing audits and semantic-D bridge, and earlier restored-sharing work including PR708. The pair-sum identity is standard. Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in reasoning, implementation, tests and writing; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
